artworks.title: Pyxis with Zeus and Aigina
artworks.description: Attic pyxis (Fitzwilliam): Zeus seizes Aegina while tradition places her father Asopus among the reacting figures — the river-god whose daughters name islands and cities, watching one stolen for the island that will bear her name.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Aegina
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum engraving from Jupiter's love adventures: the abduction of Asopus' daughter Aegina — the river-god's household rewritten as a Mannerist amorous series.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Aegina
artworks.description: Another impression of the Jupiter–Aegina pursuit: Asopus' daughter as the prize — the river-father's loss that founds the Aeacid island line.

artworks.title: Aegina Waiting for the Arrival of Zeus
artworks.description: Bol paints Asopus' daughter awaiting Zeus — the naiad whose abduction will make her father search the earth and quarrel with the king of gods.

popCulture.title: Asopus
popCulture.description: River-god of Boeotia and the Peloponnese — father of Aegina, Salamis, Thebe, Sinope and many other eponymous naiads.

popCulture.title: Aegina (mythology)
popCulture.description: Asopus' most famous daughter — mother of Aeacus, grandmother-line of Achilles, and namesake of the Saronic island.
